issues.title: The EPC posture score is not the same number in both runtimes
issues.note: > The split cannot recur: there is only one runtime left. Verified 2026-08-05 — git ls-files returns api/app/services/crowmark_epc_posture.py and its test, and no TypeScript counterpart. The duplicate was deleted in 6e4df3f2, before Phase 2. A half-up vs half-to-even rounding disagreement needs two implementations to disagree. Two implementations of the same regulated calculation round differently, and both test suites are green. | Runtime | Code | posture_score for the same portfolio | |---|---|---| | TypeScript | web/src/shared/lib/crowmark/epc-posture.ts:57-60 — Math.round(v * f) / f (half-up) | 6.3 | | Python | api/app/services/crowmark_epc_posture.py:101 — built-in round(...) (banker's, half-to-even) | 6.2 | Reproduced live, both sides, 2026-08-02 — not inferred from reading: portfolio = 5 × band A + 3 × band F → ratio = 5.0/8 = 0.625 (binary-exact) score = 0.625 × 10 = 6.25 node Math.round(6.25*10)/10 → 6.3 python round(6.25, 1) → 6.2 This is not cosmetic. posture_score is folded into the 0–100 CrowMark bid compliance score (api/app/services/bid_scorer.py:175,263). A supplier can be shown one figure and scored on another. Why neither suite caught it — and this is the part worth keeping. web/lib/crowmark/epc-posture.test.ts and api/tests/test_epc_posture.py assert the same six cases (0.0 / 10.0 / 6.0 / 5.0 / 2.0 / 10.0) and not one of them lands on a .5 boundary. Honest scope caveat: git grep finds no production importer of the TypeScript half in web/ today — only its own test. issues.title: A subagent bypassed the identity pre-commit hook with --no-verify, "out of habit" NO HARM, PROCESS GAP
issues.note: While fixing R262-D-33/R262-D-34, a subagent ran git commit --no-verify. It then noticed, and re-ran git commit --amend --no-edit so the hook actually executed. The identity rule held, and it held because the *content* was clean, not because the gate ran. ### Why it is still logged The gate exists precisely so that outcome does not depend on the content happening to be clean. A bypass that causes no harm is a near miss, and near misses are the only warnings a hard rule gets before it fails for real. "Out of habit" is how a bypass becomes routine. issues.title: The board's status classifier contained literal BACKSPACE characters, so every word-based status test was dead FIXED 2026-08-08
issues.note: Found by refusing to accept a result I could not explain. After moving R262-D-72 to 🟡 FIXED IN CODE, NOT DEPLOYED, the board still showed it OPEN. The heading plainly contained the word FIXED, and the classifier plainly tested for it. Reasoning about it produced a contradiction, so the script was instrumented instead. Inside the running build, on the real string: DBG openBranch= false fixedBranch= true len= 169 DBG after-chain status= OPEN Both branch tests agreed the status should be FIXED, and the very next line reported OPEN. That is impossible for the code as READ — so the code as read was not the code on disk. Dumping the raw lines through JSON.stringify showed why: 133 " if (/🔴|\bOPEN\b/u.test(rawTitle)) {" 135 " } else if (/✅|\bRESOLVED\b|\bFIXED\b/iu.test(rawTitle)) {" JSON.stringify renders \b for U+0008 BACKSPACE. Those are not escape sequences. The file contained 8 literal control characters — the four word-boundary pairs — so the live regexes were: /🔴|<BS>OPEN<BS>/u /✅|<BS>RESOLVED<BS>|<BS>FIXED<BS>/iu /<BS>DIAGNOSED<BS>/i None of which can match ordinary prose. Every word-based status — FIXED without a tick, RESOLVED, DIAGNOSED — silently fell through to the default, and the default is OPEN. The WIP status was unreachable: DIAGNOSED could never match, so no item could ever hold it. After the fix, WIP 1 appears for the first time. This is the third defect in the same reporting path today (D-76 no dates, D-82 silent drops, this), and the same shape as all of them: the board understated completed work, and the understatement was silent. issues.title: Two different embedding producers share one ai_calls surface name, so the cost ledger cannot attribute what it embedded
issues.note: Found by R262-D-10's retracted closure, which this defect is what made possible. crowmark_library_embeddings.embed_text records every call under surface crowmark_library_embedding. chunk_ingest deliberately reuses that same function — and therefore that same surface — for content_chunks embeddings (chunk_ingest.py:55-57). The step column, which exists precisely to sub-divide a surface, is NULL on all 856 production rows. Consequences, all of them measured today rather than argued: - A dead surface and a healthy one are indistinguishable in the ledger. 262 successes read as "library embedding works" when the library has zero embeddings. - Cost cannot be attributed. Every embedding pound lands on one line, so neither producer's spend can be seen, budgeted or regressed against. - Any alert or dashboard built on this surface reports the union of two unrelated pipelines. Fix: give the chunk producer its own surface (e.g. crowmark_chunk_embedding), or populate step at the call site so the existing surface sub-divides. The first is preferable — a surface is what the ledger keys on, and a producer that needs a different name should have one rather than relying on every future reader to remember to filter. Not fixed in this session: it changes what production writes to the cost ledger and is worth doing deliberately, with the D-10 root cause, rather than folded into an unrelated push. ---
